claim: The Alba International White Truffle Fair runs 10 October to 6 December 2026, with the World Truffle Market every weekend at the Cortile della Maddalena and tickets around 5.25 euro.
quote: the fair takes place from 10th October to 6th December 2026... The World Truffle Market will take place every weekend between 10th October and 6th December 2026 at the Cortile della Maddalena in Alba.

claim: The truffle fair pairs white truffle with Barolo and Barbera, hazelnuts, slow-cooked meats and polenta, plus cooking demonstrations, truffle dinners and producer stalls in the old town.
quote: Barolo and Barbera alongside hazelnuts, slow-cooked meats and buttery polenta make each truffle bite pop. Beyond food there are artisan stalls, old town squares full of chatter, live music and chances to meet producers.

claim: Ferrero was founded by Pietro Ferrero in Alba in 1925; Nutella began as Supercrema in 1949 and was renamed Nutella in 1964, and the factory along the Tanaro River does not permit public tours or have a public outlet store.
quote: Ferrero was founded by Pietro Ferrero in Alba in 1925... renamed to Nutella in 1964... As of April 2023, the Ferrero chocolate factory in Alba has never allowed the general public onto its premises... outlet shop open only to employees and law enforcement personnel.

claim: Alba is the birthplace of Nutella and Ferrero Rocher and is known for gianduja, a blend of chocolate and local Tonda Gentile hazelnuts; though the factory cannot be toured, you can smell the chocolate near it and buy Nutella cakes, ice cream and bakery treats in town.
quote: Alba, the Italian town where Nutella and Ferrero Rocher were born... known for its exquisite chocolate, particularly the famed gianduja... the Ferrero factory itself is impossible to tour... it's in the center of the town of Alba and you can smell the chocolate if you get close enough.

claim: The Enoteca Regionale Piemontese Cavour, set in the 13th-century Grinzane Cavour Castle just outside Alba, was established in 1967 as the first regional enoteca in Piedmont and stocks Piedmontese wines, grappas and food products, open 10am to 6pm.
quote: The Enoteca (wine shop) was set up in 1967, the first in Piedmont and the second of its kind in Italy... the Selection of the Order of the Knights of the Truffle and Alba Wines has been reserved exclusively for the wineries that are members of the Enoteca.

claim: Petricore Enoteca con Cucina in Alba is a wine bar with a deep Piedmont selection sourced from well-connected local producers (including rare bottles like a 2010 Barolo Chinato) plus a capable wine-forward kitchen.
quote: The Petricore Enoteca team are clearly well-connected to nearby Piedmont wine producers... a rare 2010 Barolo Chinato with only 1,000 bottles made annually... that place that is both a bar and yet a sensible restaurant.

claim: Alba town has multiple wine bars and enotecas for in-town tasting, including Enoteca Fracchia & Berchialla, Voglia di Vino (a wine bar/shop/restaurant with 400+ bottles from 150 producers and 60+ wines by the glass) and the Roberto Sarotto tasting room on Piazza Savona.
quote: Voglia di Vino is a combination wine bar, wine shop and restaurant in Alba with wine shop shelves stocked with over 400 different bottles of wine from 150 producers with more than 60 wines available by the glass.
